name: Hochfilzen
kurzbeschreibung: Known as the Biathlon hub with the Biathlon-Arena Hochfilzen and the Pillersee course.
beschreibung:
Overview

Hochfilzen is situated at an altitude of 959 metres in the easternmost corner of the Kitzbühel district, directly on the provincial border with Salzburg at the Grießen Pass (975 m). Nestled between the craggy ridges of the Lofer and Leogang Mountains to the north and the gentler slopes of the Kitzbühel Alps to the south, the peaceful village has around 1,300 residents. Thanks to its special basin topography, Hochfilzen is widely celebrated as Tyrol's proverbial snow haven, enjoying an exceptionally long and reliable winter season. The mountain village gained international fame as a world-class biathlon venue, hosting prestigious World Championships and the annual IBU Biathlon World Cup. Beyond the excitement of elite sports, Hochfilzen has preserved its tranquil, genuine alpine village charm, delighting outdoor lovers and families throughout the scenic PillerseeTal.

History

The first documented record of the settlement dates back to 1377 in an estate register of the Bavarian monastery of Rott under the name ze Hochviltzen. For centuries, the area belonged to the Pillersee estate administered by the Kitzbühel district court. While mining had early roots here, a defining modern milestone occurred in 1957 with the establishment of industrial magnesite mining. To this day, RHI Magnesita extracts high-grade raw magnesite from open-cast and underground mines at Weißenstein and Bürgl. Another historic breakthrough was the completion of the Empress Elisabeth Railway (Giselabahn) in 1875, connecting Hochfilzen to the European rail network. The spiritual heart of the village is the Parish and Pilgrimage Church of Maria Schnee (Our Lady of the Snows), which originated from a 1682 Loreto chapel founded by miners and was expanded into a beautiful Baroque church.

Getting There

Hochfilzen boasts outstanding transport links by both road and rail. Motorists arriving from Innsbruck or Munich take the Inntal Motorway A12 or A8/A93, continuing past St. Johann in Tirol and Fieberbrunn along the B164 Hochkönig federal highway. From the east, the B164 leads directly from Saalfelden and Leogang across the Grießen Pass, which remains open year-round. Rail travellers enjoy effortless access: Hochfilzen railway station is a key stop along the Salzburg-Tyrol Railway, served regularly by Tyrol S-Bahn line S8 and regional trains, ensuring a comfortable, car-free journey straight into the mountains.

Tips

During the winter months, Hochfilzen is a Nordic sports paradise. A vast network of immaculately groomed cross-country tracks spans the high plateau, seamlessly connecting to neighbouring Fieberbrunn and St. Ulrich am Pillersee. Visitors can test their marksmanship and skiing prowess during guest biathlon workshops. In summer, the Buchensteinwand beckons with the remarkable St. Jakob Cross (Jakobskreuz): Standing 30 metres high at 1,456 metres altitude, this accessible cruciform structure offers four panoramic viewing decks with vistas sweeping from the Wilder Kaiser to the High Tauern. Hikers also relish ascents to the Spielbergalm or challenging via ferratas across the Leogang Mountains.
